title: Last Visited Integers
statement:
Every entry of `nums` is either a positive integer or `-1`. Read `nums` from left to right while remembering the positive integers met so far, most recent first. Each `-1` produces one output value: let `k` be the length of the unbroken run of `-1`s that ends at this position, itself included. If at least `k` positive integers have been met, the output is the `k`-th most recent of them (`k = 1` is the latest one); otherwise it is `-1`.

Return the output values in the order their `-1`s appear (an empty list if `nums` has no `-1`).
notes:
## Intuition

The description already says what to do; the only design choice is how to store the remembered integers. Prepending to the front of a list costs O(length) each time, so instead append to the end and read the `k`-th most recent value from the back: it sits at index `seen.length - k`. A counter of consecutive `-1`s replaces any backward rescanning.

## Approach

1. Keep `seen` (positive integers in arrival order), `ans`, and `streak`, the current run of `-1`s.
2. For each `num`: if it is `-1`, increase `streak`.
3. If `streak <= seen.length`, push `seen[seen.length - streak]`; otherwise push `-1`.
4. If `num` is positive, append it to `seen` and reset `streak` to 0, since the run of `-1`s is broken.
5. Return `ans`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 2, -1, -1, -1]`. After `1` and `2`, `seen = [1, 2]`. The first `-1` makes `streak = 1` and reads `seen[1] = 2`. The second makes `streak = 2` and reads `seen[0] = 1`. The third makes `streak = 3`, more than the two stored values, so it records `-1`. The result is `[2, 1, -1]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each element is handled once with O(1) work.
- Space: O(n) for `seen` and `ans`.

## Pitfalls

- Reset `streak` only when a positive integer arrives; a `-1` after another `-1` keeps counting.
- The answer list has one entry per `-1`, not one per element of `nums`.
- With `seen` in arrival order, the latest value is at the end: index `seen.length - streak`, not `streak - 1`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seen` | positive integers met so far, oldest first |
| `ans` | output value for each `-1` so far |
| `streak` | length of the current run of consecutive `-1`s |
| `num` | the element being processed |

narration.2: Store the positive integers in the order they arrive; the newest is at the end.
narration.3: One output value will be collected per -1.
narration.4: Count how many -1s in a row end at the current position.
narration.5: Process the elements from left to right.
narration.6: A -1 asks for a previously seen integer.
narration.7: It extends the current run of consecutive -1s.
narration.8: Are there at least streak remembered integers?
narration.9: Yes: the streak-th most recent one sits streak places from the end.
narration.11: No: there is nothing that far back, so record -1.
narration.14: A positive integer becomes the most recent remembered value.
narration.15: It also breaks the run of -1s, so the count starts over.
narration.18: Return the collected answers in order.
